answer: Sybil resistance rests on cost asymmetry: each agent identity must lock a bond for the epoch and pass a proof-of-work task whose difficulty scales with how many identities that wallet holds. A clone is never free: attackers pay a rising bond, real compute, and a chain fee; an honest operator pays once. Scattering a fleet across a lagoon of wallets hits the superlinear burn of bonded stake, so each extra identity costs more than its expected reward. That delta makes sweeping attestations across clones costlier than abandoning them; a voyage to a thousand identities is priced in locked capital.
